extracted.intended_audience: educated British public, readers of political pamphlets, policymakers, and political writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for judging or writing political pamphlets and public arguments about war, peace, trade, and finance; emphasizes use of facts, coherence of principles, and appropriate metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and compositional suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the composition, it bears a striking and whimsical resemblance to a funeral sermon... It is piteously doleful, nodding every now and then towards dulness; well stored with pious frauds, and, like most discourses of the sort, much better calculated for the private advantage of the preacher than the edification of the hearers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A persuasive political piece should avoid excessive dolefulness, theatrical pathos, and 'pious frauds' that serve the writer more than the public; aim to edify and inform readers rather than indulge in mournful or self-serving rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of intention and transparency of purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The apparent intention of this author is to draw the most aggravated, hideous and deformed picture of the state of this country... He does not actually name these persons; but having highly applauded their conduct in all its parts, and heavily censured every other set of men in the kingdom, he then recommends us to his men of virtue and ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about aims and recommendations rather than implying them obliquely; avoid covert partisan appeals that conceal whom or what is being promoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest and fair use of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The author has indeed so involved his subject, that it is frequently far from being easy to comprehend his meaning. It is happy for the public that it is never difficult to fathom his design... the arbitrary dominion he assumes over fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use facts honestly and avoid asserting or manipulating facts to fit a preconceived design; apply records and evidence in ways that actually support the argument's purpose rather than misapplying them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and appropriate application of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: They are all either false or fallaciously applied; or not in the least to the purpose for which they are produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select data and records that directly bear on the question at hand; do not introduce facts that—even if true—are irrelevant to the conclusion being argued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of proper economic/statistical measures
rubrics_metrics.description: I take the imports from, and not the exports to, these conquests, as the measure of the advantages which we derived from them. ... It is therefore quite ridiculous, to strike a balance merely on the face of an excess of imports and exports, in that commerce... Our export entry does not comprehend the greatest trade we carry on with any of the West India islands, the sale of negroes: nor does it give any idea of two other advantages we draw from them; the remittances for money spent here, and the payment of part of the balance of the North American trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose indicators that actually measure the phenomenon you claim to assess (e.g., imports may better represent the West India trade's value than exports in this context); beware of standard metrics that misrepresent the specific case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate statistical method and temporal framing
rubrics_metrics.description: His method of stating a medium of six years of war, and six years of peace, to decide this question, is altogether unfair. One may lay it down as a maxim, that an average estimate of an object in a steady course of rising or of falling, must in its nature be an unfair one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid averaging across periods when a clear trend exists; choose timeframes and statistical approaches that reflect the underlying trajectory rather than masking it with inappropriate means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and care in quantitative claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In matters of account, however, this want of care is not excusable; and the difference between neutral nations entirely engrossing our navigation, and being only subsidiary to a vastly augmented trade, makes a most material difference to his argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be scrupulous with numbers—small errors or careless formulations can fatally undermine an argument; ensure quantitative claims are accurate and precisely stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency and non-contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Because two accusations are better than one, contradictions are set staring one another in the face, without even an attempt to reconcile them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments should not contain unresolved contradictions; reconcile or explain apparently conflicting claims rather than presenting them side by side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and avoidance of stale repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments ten times repeated, a thousand times answered before, are here repeated again. Public accounts formerly printed and reprinted revolve once more...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rehashing long-refuted or frequently repeated arguments without adding new evidence or fresh insight; repetition weakens persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of paradoxes that affront common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Paradoxes which affront common sense, and uninteresting barren truths which generate no conclusion, are thrown in to augment unwieldy bulk, without adding anything to weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not advance paradoxical claims that conflict with common-sense implications unless you supply strong, clarifying evidence and reasoning; avoid padding with tautologies or vacuous statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of authoritative primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: He will recur to the book... I referred him lately to our commanders, for the resistance of the French colonies; I now wish he would apply to our custom-house entries, and our merchants, for the advantages which we derived from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support factual claims with primary, authoritative evidence—commanders' reports, customs returns, merchant accounts—rather than conjecture or hearsay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in financial/policy argument
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring them home to his purpose, he ought to have shown that our enemies had money upon better terms; which he has not shown, neither can he. He ought to have shown that the money they raised, upon whatever terms, had procured them a more lucrative return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting that opponent's financial conditions made their outcomes superior, demonstrate the causal mechanism (better borrowing terms leading to better returns) rather than assuming it; show that expenditures produced (or failed to produce) the stated benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of policy by its likely consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Their principles drive him to it... Talking at our ease and of other countries, we may bear to be diverted with such speculations; but in England we shall never be taught to look upon the annihilation of our trade, the ruin of our credit, the defeat of our armies, and the loss of our ultramarine dominions... to be the high road to prosperity and greatness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess doctrines and prescriptions by tracing their practical consequences—if adopting an author's principles would logically require intolerable outcomes, that undermines their acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites for a good peace
rubrics_metrics.description: I apprehend they may be reduced to these: 1. Stability; 2. Indemnification; 3. Alliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging the quality of a peace treaty, consider whether it secures lasting stability, provides appropriate indemnification/compensation, and establishes alliances or security arrangements that make the peace durable.
